comparison.sigma_drop_from_18_deletions: CONTROLLED back-to-back (run A3 current 155 then run C2 pre-retire 173, both in clean GO windows, close in time): ΔΣ = -308.6s = -8.2% (A3 3467.0s vs C2 3775.7s). This is the best estimate for 'how much the 18 deletions reduced Σ'. Significance: the controlled run-to-run variance of the current suite (A2 3734 vs A3 3467, both GO-started = 267s) and the old same-condition noise (~167s) bracket the ΔΣ; -309s is ~1.2-1.9x that noise = MARGINAL (not clearly significant, but no longer 'within ±1000s noise'). The earlier ±1000s+ was HALF the raw range of 3 runs (2471-4836) that MIXED conditions (run B memory-degraded at swap ~1.4GB) - an UPPER bound, not the controlled noise. Gross Σ of the 18 deleted files: >=207s from the two in run C top-20 (prepare-milestone-convergence 137.7s, execute-milestone-worktree 69.2s) + 16 others each <56.6s.
comparison.wall_clock: outer measured scripts/test.sh wall 562.3s -> 569.1s (+1.2%, no drop); node --test wall here 403-700s (current) vs 563.4s (pre-retire), within noise
comparison.conclusion: Controlled back-to-back shows Σ dropped ~8.2% (-309s) after removing 18 test files / 402 tests - marginal (noise ~167-267s). My node --test wall also dropped ~6.8% (A3 498.8s vs C2 535.1s), but the outer's scripts/test.sh wall went +1.2% (562.3->569.1s) - so the Σ drop does NOT translate to a proportionate wall drop (the outer's wall didn't drop at all). The correction stands: cli.test.mjs is ~4.9% of Σ, not 34.8% of wall. The suite is 8-lane saturated; a file's cost must be measured against Σ, not wall clock. Net: the 18 deletions bought at most ~8% Σ and 0-7% wall - far below the ~35% the wrong denominator implied.
